quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You are parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels so the car will roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail. Do this when parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.
Use your high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep the dashboard lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day. You cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop your car within the distance your headlights illuminate.

questions.question: You can legally turn left at a red traffic light after stopping only if:

options.text: You are on a two-way street turning onto a two-way street.
You are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you may turn left at a red light only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street. Check for signs that prohibit this turn.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, you should:

options.text: Look toward the center of the road.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on course. Do not keep your bright lights on to retaliate.

questions.question: You are in the left lane of two lanes going your direction. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. A driver behind you wants to go faster. You should:

options.text: Stay in your lane so traffic flows smoothly.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let other vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to pass, turn left, or drive fast. Use the right lane when driving slower than surrounding traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. You must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles also turning left.
All approaching vehicles.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a walk signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All approaching vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other vehicles moving on their green light.

questions.question: If it feels like your tires have lost grip on the road, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting to a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Ease your foot off the gas pedal and stay off the brakes. Do not try to stop or turn until your tires are gripping the road again.

questions.question: Which of the following is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas on a road freeze before and thaw after other parts of the road. On cold, wet days, these spots become icy.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning while driving in the rain, you should:

options.text: Drive at a speed appropriate for good conditions.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When driving too fast in wet conditions, your tires may lose contact with the road. Your car will ride on top of the water, called hydroplaning. Drive slower in rain or wet conditions to prevent this.

questions.question: If a driver passes you in a no passing zone, you should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Maintain your speed and position.
Slow down and let the other driver safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the other driver safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Passing areas depend on how far ahead drivers can see. Help the passing vehicle return to your lane safely so everyone can avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: Which statement about work zones is true?

options.text: Fines for work zone violations are the same as regular traffic violations.
You must slow down in work zones.
Only slow down if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down in work zones.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop for road equipment. Driving safely through work zones protects drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and road workers.

questions.question: If your vehicle skids to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Do not turn the steering wheel.
Turn the steering wheel to the left.
Turn the steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, release the gas pedal, do not brake, and steer in the direction of the skid. If your car has anti-lock brakes, press the brakes firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: How do you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Switch to another lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Switch to another lane.
questions.explanation: Create space for vehicles entering the freeway. If possible, change lanes to give them room. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed so they can enter safely and smoothly.

questions.question: When parallel parking, how far should you be from the curb?

options.text: Three feet
Two feet
One foot

questions.correctAnswerText: One foot
questions.explanation: Park with your wheels parallel to the curb and within one foot of it. Only park where it will not block traffic and where drivers can see your car from both directions.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down.
Flash your headlights.
Honk your horn sharply.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn sharply.
questions.explanation: Use a sharp horn blast when danger is present. Do this when a child or any pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are driving.
Stop only if you are driving in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are driving.
questions.explanation: Come to a complete stop before reaching a school bus that is picking up or dropping off passengers, regardless of your direction of travel.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you arrive at the same time as vehicles on your right and left, you should:

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until all vehicles have left before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: When multiple vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the right has the right-of-way. Other drivers proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: You are driving the wrong way.
Treat it like a stop sign.
Do not go until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should:

options.text: Watch for traffic coming from the right.
Merge right.
Turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic coming from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert you to hazards ahead and are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that traffic will merge into their lane from the right.

questions.question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?

options.text: Stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go.
Slow down and continue with caution.
Stop and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop fully and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions coming up ahead. This sign warns drivers about a curve to the right.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this red and white sign?

options.text: Stop and look both ways before proceeding.
Let traffic on the road ahead pass before you proceed.
Keep your speed steady and watch for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic on the road ahead pass before you proceed.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop if needed. Let other vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians pass first. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Slow down by easing off the gas pedal and using light brake pressure.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check for other drivers in your way. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Never change lanes or pass in an intersection.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should not:

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on the road or shoulder if you miss your exit. Continue to the next exit instead. Other drivers do not expect vehicles backing up on the highway, and this causes collisions.
